ls_provost.text: It's a splendid hall, if I say so myself. The windows are my favourites, with the Norse earls in their helmets. Up Helly Aa's feast is held in halls like this one, after the burning: the squads go from hall to hall all night, performing a short act at each, and drinking something warming at every stop.
By the end, it's a sight. Dozens of squads, a dozen halls. Everyone ends up in the wrong hall at least once. Nobody minds.

then.text: Whatever the isle asks, I will put it to the committee with my name on it. I will recommend what I can defend, and I will say what I could not.
Tell Eila I would give her the full boat if the pot allowed. That is not a line. That is arithmetic.

else.text: Ruth Leask. I do transport for the council, which means I say no to people who are right.

The isle boat is old and costs more per passenger than anything else we run. It needs replacing within a few years, and the money for lifeline services is one pot, shared between a dozen isles. Every pound for this boat is a pound I cannot give to another isle's boat, or to the school bus on the north Mainland.

I am not asking the isle to be grateful. I am asking them to tell me which loss they can live with. A smaller boat, or fewer days, or the full service and somebody else's bus. There is no fourth option, and I have looked.
Please, sit. I have thirty-one emails and six of them are polite.
